html:
An Eastern Roman empress who steered the court of her younger brother, Theodosius II. In 414, at fifteen, she became his guardian and was named Augusta. She and her sisters took vows of virginity and made the palace almost like a convent.

She chose her brother's bride, the learned Eudocia, and pushed church affairs hard. She opposed the bishop Nestorius, who would not call Mary the Mother of God, and backed his condemnation at the Council of Ephesus in 431.

When Theodosius died in 450 there was no male heir. Pulcheria married the officer Marcian, on terms that let her keep her vow, and made him emperor. With him she called the Council of Chalcedon in 451, which defined the two natures of Christ. She died in 453 and is honoured as a saint.
